params.title: IRC Channel Activity with Minimal Engagement
params.description: Mr. Evil's IRC account (mrevilrulez) joined channels with hacker-oriented names including #elite.hackers, #evilfork (EFnet), and #chataholics (UnderNet) on August 20, 2004. However, analysis of the actual IRC logs shows minimal activity: #elite.hackers session lasted 4 minutes (10:45-10:49) with only music playing by other users; #chataholics session lasted 2 minutes (10:52-10:54) with only one message from mrevilrulez ("glib marm"). No evidence of actual hacking discussions or coordination found in the logs. All IRC activity appears to be routine chat, not substantive participation in hacker communities. Activity was brief and contained no technical hacking-related content.

params.title: Greg Schardt ("Mr. Evil") Maintained Organized Hacking Toolkit on Dell Laptop
params.description: User "Mr. Evil" on Dell_Latitude_CPi system is definitively identified as Greg Schardt via Yahoo account URL (edit.yahoo.com/config with .fn=Greg, .ln=Schardt, .id=mrevil2000). System contained extensive organized toolkit in My Documents folders: FOOTPRINTING/NT (Nmap, NSTPro2, SuperScan, spade114), ENUMERATION/NT (ogre), EXPLOITATION/Unix (dsniff 2.3). Installed tools include Ethereal (packet analyzer, executed 2004-08-27 15:34:54), Cain & Abel (password recovery, executed 2004-08-27 15:33:02), NetStumbler (WiFi scanner, executed 2004-08-27 15:12:35), Whois, Look@LAN, Agent newsreader. User accessed http://www.wardriving.com/ on 2004-08-27. Directory naming structure (FOOTPRINTING, ENUMERATION, EXPLOITATION) suggests systematic preparation for network reconnaissance and exploitation activities. WinPcap driver installed to support packet capture. Tools executed between August 20-27, 2004. No evidence found of actual data exfiltration or successful attacks, only capability and tool preparation.
